threads.body: Weaver 0.27 changes the `--output http` shutdown protocol: `POST /stop` no longer returns the report, and clients must fetch `GET /report` and then call `POST /shutdown`. The runner delegates this lifecycle to `opentelemetry.test.weaver_live_check.WeaverLiveCheck.end()`, while its declared dependency still allows versions as old as `opentelemetry-test-utils 0.65b0`, whose client predates this protocol. Such a valid installation will fail when ending every scenario. Please update the runner dependency to the first test-utils version supporting Weaver 0.27 (or update the lifecycle implementation) together with this pin.

replies.body:
No code change.

Already addressed before the frozen head by commit 953dde8001ec15c4522bc3e068e2098f13004d19. tools/runner/src/opentelemetry/conformance/_session.py:212-214 imports the runner-local WeaverLiveCheck subclass, whose _do_stop override in _weaver.py:21-54 uses POST /stop, GET /report, and POST /shutdown for Weaver 0.27 and preserves legacy report-returning /stop behavior. Inspection of test-utils 0.65b0 confirms its inherited end() dispatches to self._do_stop(), and all nine lifecycle test cases pass with exactly that declared minimum version. Raising the dependency floor is therefore unnecessary.

threads.body: `check_weaver()` still accepts Weaver 0.26.1 with only a warning (`_registry.py:189–214`). That version returns the report from `/stop` and exits, so this unconditional `/report` request fails instead of returning the scenario report. Use the legacy lifecycle for pre-0.27 versions, or reject incompatible versions before starting the scenario.

+# Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Weaver live-check lifecycle for the version pinned by this repo."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+
+from requests import get, post
+
+from opentelemetry.test.weaver_live_check import LiveCheckReport
+from opentelemetry.test.weaver_live_check import (
+    WeaverLiveCheck as _WeaverLiveCheck,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class WeaverLiveCheck(_WeaverLiveCheck):
+    # test-utils still expects /stop to return the report and exit the process.
+    def _do_stop(self, timeout: int) -> tuple[LiveCheckReport, int]:
+        if not self._ready:
+            raise RuntimeError("WeaverLiveCheck process did not start successfully")
+        try:
+            base_url = f"http://localhost:{self._admin_port}"
+            response = post(f"{base_url}/stop", timeout=timeout)
+            response.raise_for_status()
+            try:
+                response = get(f"{base_url}/report", timeout=timeout)

threads.body: This import follows the executable `pytest.importorskip()` call, violating E402, which is enabled by `pyproject.toml:14`. The lint job runs `ruff check .` (`.github/workflows/runner.yml:66–69`), so this blocks CI. Suppress E402 on this deliberately delayed import.

replies.body:
No code change.

The claimed E402 failure is not reproducible with Ruff 0.17.0. The configured CI step at .github/workflows/runner.yml:66-69 runs ruff check . without pinning an older Ruff version. That exact check passes, and ruff check --isolated --no-cache --select E402 tools/runner/tests/test_weaver.py also passes. An isolated stdin control accepts an import after pytest.importorskip but reports E402 after an ordinary print call, demonstrating that Ruff recognizes the deliberate optional-dependency guard rather than disabling the rule. Adding a suppression would be unnecessary.

threads.body: Both new lifecycle tests are skipped by the CI unit-test job: `.github/workflows/runner.yml:41–52` omits `opentelemetry-test-utils` and installs the runner with `--no-deps`. The coverage-model job installs the dependencies, but its pytest command (lines 301–304) does not include `tools/runner/tests`. Add this file to that command so CI checks both the shutdown sequence and cleanup after a report failure.
